what: Ask for a Play Store rating inside the app (Google's own in-app review card) at a happy moment: a new personal best or the 10th finished workout, at most once in a few months
why: The phone app has no in-app rating ask anywhere in its Android parts, so the Play listing gets ratings only from members who go looking; the happy moments are already known to the app
impact_why: Ratings and their count drive Play search rank and the install rate of every gym's invite link; this is the cheapest lever on store conversion
my_view: My view: do it. One small native call, shown after a PR or a milestone, never after a failed save. The store listing text itself belongs to the store area; this is only the ask.

what: Make the rest timer an Android 16 "Live Update": the countdown shows as a chip in the status bar and at the top of the lock screen, not only inside the notification list
why: Today the rest card is an ordinary notification with a drawn countdown; on Android 16 Google promotes timers like this to a status bar chip, which Google Clock already uses (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Rest is the most-seen moment of every workout; seeing seconds left without pulling down the shade saves a swipe each set
my_view: My view: worth it, keep the current card for older phones. Test on his phone first; what the watch copies must not change.

what: Add a third app-icon shortcut "Check in" that opens the gym poster scanner, for members who have joined a gym
why: The long-press menu holds only Start (or Resume) and Log body weight, though up to four fit; checking in today means open app, Gym tab, scan, and only the "Gym right now" widget skips that, which few members add
impact_why: Every gym visit starts with a check-in; one long-press instead of three taps at the gym door
my_view: My view: do it. The scanner link already exists for the widget; show it only to members in a gym.

what: Let the "Time to train" reminder say what to beat today ("Push 1 · try Bench 62.5 kg x 8"), the same line the Today widget already shows
why: The reminder only says "Next: Push 1" or "Open MettleUp to start your workout", easy to swipe away; a concrete target is a reason to go
impact_why: Reminders are the one push every opted-in member gets on training days; a specific target lifts the tap rate
my_view: My view: do it. Reuse the widget's what-to-beat line word for word (never a new guess); keep the plain line when there is no last time.

what: When Plus is switched on, let the app show a free trial set up in Play (for example 7 days) instead of only the base price
why: The pay code picks only the plain base plan and skips every Play offer, so a free trial or launch discount set up in Play would never reach the member
impact_why: A free trial is the usual way fitness apps such as Strong and Hevy turn free members into payers (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live); behind a switch today, so no member is affected yet
my_view: My view: decide before Plus goes live; a small change once he picks a trial length. Money wording must pass member-words first.

what: On the Today widget, when there is no plan or the plan day has no exercises, make the button "Start" (an empty workout) instead of "Open"
why: A member with no plan sees "No plan yet / Open MettleUp to start a workout" and must open the app, find the Workout tab and press Start; the widget could start it in one tap
impact_why: Saves two taps for members who train without a plan, a common way to begin
my_view: My view: do it with the same one-time key the Start button already uses, so no other app can start a workout.

what: Send each lift's sets and reps to Health Connect with the workout, not only "Strength training" with a start, end and calories
why: Google Health and Samsung Health show a MettleUp workout as a bare block; Health Connect can hold the exercise parts and reps, so members who live in those apps see what they trained
impact_why: Matters to members who use Samsung Health or Fitbit as their main record
my_view: My view: later. Nice for trust, but each lift must map to Health Connect's fixed exercise list; do it only if members ask.

what: Offer "Add <gym> to your home screen" once more at a good moment (the first real check-in at the gym), not only once after joining
why: The gym logo shortcut is the gym's own icon on the member's phone, the most visible piece of gym branding; it is asked for in one place and never again
impact_why: A gym icon on the home screen keeps the gym, and the app, in daily sight; owners pay for that branding
my_view: My view: do it, once per member, after the first check-in; never more than twice in total.
